host.instance: AWS Lightsail csx-prod-1, bundle small_3_0, 2 vCPU burstable / 2 GB RAM

findings.title: Package detail pages return 503 'database busy' for the large majority of requests
findings.mechanism: Three stacked admission layers each with a ~250ms budget: withPackageLoadSlot (4 slots, 250ms), the interactive pool (CSX_DB_READ_CONNS=2, CSX_DB_READ_WAIT=250ms), and snapshotLoadRetryDefer (15s post-failure blackout). Under builder CPU contention the underlying snapshot read takes 10-36s, so no request can hold a slot long enough to fill the 30-minute package cache, and the cache can only be filled by a request that succeeds.
findings.classification: server+DB, not browser, not payload, not cold-start

findings.title: Production host has exhausted Lightsail CPU burst capacity and is clamped to 20% baseline

evidence.cpuUtilization: exactly 20.00 avg with 20.03-20.14 max for days at a time - a throttle ceiling, not a workload shape
evidence.onlyRecoveryWindow: 2026-09-12T15:00 through 2026-09-13T15:00, burst recovered to 56.41% and CPU rose to 32-51% avg, then burned back to zero

findings.title: Compatibility builder consumes ~0.9 vCPU continuously at a 78% duty cycle, starving every request path

evidence.dutyCycle: 201 of 257 wall-clock minutes busy between 09:39 and 13:56 = 78%
evidence.interval: CSX_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL=5m - the gap between passes, not the period
evidence.projectsOwnMeasurement: cmd/csx-server/webstore.go: the snapshot read costs 0.59s with the builder idle and 36.5s while a builder pass runs - 62x, all buffer hits, CPU contention not disk

findings.classification: aggregation/rebuild work colliding with request paths

findings.title: Production pool policy is 3x tighter on connections and 12x tighter on wait than the shipped default

findings.title: builder_purl_coord SQL function costs 16.5ms per evaluation and is maintained on expression indexes over the two hottest write tables
Sequential scans read ~55 billion tuples from tables of 8k-320k rows
csx-server runs permanently above GOMEMLIMIT, so the Go collector is in continuous back-to-back GC

evidence.goRuntimeBehaviour: above the soft limit the collector runs continuously, capped by the runtime at 50% of GOMAXPROCS (=2 here, so up to 1 core)
